problem: When rollout GPUs sit in a different datacenter from the trainer, shipping the full new model weights after every update takes minutes to over an hour, which is longer than the training step itself.
who_pays: frontier labs running disaggregated or cross-region agentic RL at 100B to 1T parameters
recipe_failure: standard full-checkpoint weight sync makes per-update refits infeasible across clusters at trillion-parameter scale
trick: NeMo-DCR exploits the fact that only about 1% of BF16 weights change per RL step: it ships just the changed elements (XOR-encoded, in the receiver's own tensor layout) with a bit-exact guarantee that the rollout engine ends up with the same bytes as a full copy, and pipelines the transfer over a relay tree so no cross-cluster collective is needed.
